originalpt
Elden Ring is FromSoftware’s masterpiece—the best game they have created to date. What I find truly incredible about it is the level of immersion it offers; every player can approach it differently. Two people could complete the game with entirely distinct experiences—having defeated different bosses, explored different areas, and followed unique paths—yet each journey carries the same profound significance. This is something a film or a series cannot achieve; only this game can. It serves as a love letter to its genre, perfectly embodying the core philosophy of Hidetaka Miyazaki.Major premise: True triumph does not stem from an easy victory, but from the meaning discovered by persevering through inevitable frustration and defeat.Minor premise: Miyazaki’s games compel the player to constantly confront death, learn from every mistake, and overcome seemingly impossible challenges.Conclusion: Therefore, the satisfaction found in Miyazaki’s works does not come from simply beating the game, but from the personal transformation you undergo by refusing to give up.

uranium319
I picked up this game without any experience with Fromsoftware games or any similar games. Now after 600 hours played over the years, I finally come here to finish my duty of giving it a review. It's simply the best game ever made. The vastness of the world. The wonder. The dread of walking around a corner in a dungeon with massive amount of runes and no flasks. The boss encounters. The rage when failing even the 30th boss attempt. The joy of finally beating the boss on my 40th try with 1hp left. And then returning to do it all over again with a different playstyle. The game has some minor downsides (like minor performance issues and graphics not being cutting-edge) but they do not matter much. The worst thing is I can never experience this again without having any clue about what is waiting for me.

Elden Ring is one of the most disappointing games I have played. The graphics are relatively beautiful, but almost everything else falls **** story is poorly presented, with little narrative direction or meaningful character development. You are thrown into a massive world and expected to explore, fight bosses, and keep moving forward without understanding why you are doing any of it. The game relies too heavily on players piecing together obscure lore instead of providing a coherent and engaging **** open world is huge but feels empty and unrewarding. Exploration often feels like wandering around without a meaningful purpose, while the combat becomes repetitive and frustrating. Boss fights revolve too much around dodging long attack sequences and waiting for brief openings to strike, making combat feel more tedious than enjoyable.Overall, the game fails to make its world, story, exploration, or combat interesting enough to keep me playing. I eventually dropped it because I was simply bored.
